summary: Author skeptical review approves a bounded additive engineering round after repairing environment isolation, broad command authority and conflation of completed checks with semantic acceptance. This is not an independent legal review.
findings: Wrong baseline: old evaluation scripts hard-code a depleted 100-call allowance. They are not executed as live comparators; current offline regression and retained round-10 evidence are used.
Proxy metric: agreement and mutation percentages cannot promote semantic correctness. Each material discrepancy remains unresolved and the release flag stays false.
Environment mismatch: tools are installed in a separate CPU virtualenv and OCR sysroot. The main environment and Catala worktree remain independent inputs.
Command scope: generic Python -m allow rules were rejected. The supervisor emits exact reviewed argv and never evaluates shell text.
Stop and repair: three failed attempts per phase, subprocess timeouts, counted discrepancy actions, immutable attempts and automatic successor refresh are required.
Shared dependencies: ResearchAssistant and direct Poppler share Poppler; Docling and pypdf share PDF text-layer risks; OCR is a distinct observation but does not prove completeness.

Artifact relevance: every source page is checked, formal reports declare the supported fragment, Inspect uses hidden deterministic targets, and PIT challenges a scoped Java control alongside generated-Java conformance.
Fairness: synthetic challenges cannot establish model ranking or reviewer-cost reduction. KeY/MAPIE and unmerged Catala remain explicit successor work.
